chunks: About a man who hears a sound at the door while he is in salat (prayer), so he clears his throat to make his servant-girl or his family hear, so that she may come to him, and he gestures to her with his hand to inform her who is at the door so that she may look and see who it is. He said: “There is no harm in that.”

And about a man and a woman who are in salat (prayer) and want something: is it permissible for them to say, “Subḥān Allāh”? He said: “Yes, and they may gesture toward what they want, and when a woman wants something, she strikes upon her thighs while she is in salat (prayer).”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act being discussed
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: an expression of glorifying Allah, used here as verbal indication during prayer
key_terms.فَيَتَنَحْنَحُ: he clears his throat in order to alert someone
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permitted
key_terms.وَيُومِيَانِ: the two of them gesture or signal

ai.seo_question: What kinds of gestures or sounds are permitted during salat (prayer) if someone needs to communicate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about limited actions during salat (prayer) when a need arises. It indicates that clearing the throat, saying “Subḥān Allāh,” and making gestures for a need do not invalidate the prayer, and it specifies that a woman may strike her thighs to indicate something while praying.
